title: Region-aware alert quiescence and runbook automation for tactical load-shedding
creator: Diego Ruiz
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a region-aware alert quiescence strategy plus automated runbook actions to reduce pager noise during transient multi-region degradations and to enable fast, safe load-shedding when SLO burn rate exceeds thresholds. The intent is to: 1) avoid wake-ups for transient region blips by combining deduplication, intent scoring, and quiet windows; 2) attach automated mitigation steps to high-confidence alerts (circuit-breaker trips, region degradation) to reduce manual toil; and 3) ensure failover/load-shedding is orchestrated with canary rollback and safe fallthroughs to lower-cost variants.

Motivation:
We continue to see the majority of pages during multi-region partial outages are noisy duplicates (same customer requests retried across regions) or low-impact SLO degradations that do not require immediate human action. Meanwhile, engineers spend time executing the same recovery steps for load-shedding and circuit isolation. Consolidating these behaviors into a region-aware quiescence policy and automated runbook actions will reduce MTTR and on-call fatigue while preserving safety and customer SLA guarantees.

Scope and deliverables:
- Design and implement a Region Alert Quiescence policy that: aggregates alerts across regions, applies de-duplication windowing, and suppresses pages for low-intent duplicative signals while surfacing a single unified incident ticket.
- Define explicit SLO/EB rules that trigger automated load-shedding and circuit breaker actions (e.g., reduce non-critical traffic by X%, enable KV cache-only routing, switch to quantized model variant) when regional error budget burn rate > 10x for 5 minutes and global burn risk is medium/high.
- Implement runbook automation hooks: webhook triggers to the runbook-runner service that can execute approved remediation steps (traffic-tier scaling, model-variant fallback, regional cutover) with an interactive approval window for P0 escalations.
- Update console dashboards (per-route SLO burn, region health timeline) and add paging-score metadata so on-call sees consolidated context.
- Author and publish a short on-call playbook with clear rollback criteria, acceptance tests, and post-incident tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A region-quiescence policy exists and is configurable per service with dedupe window and suppression thresholds
Pages are reduced by >=30% on known multi-region transient incidents in the next 30-day experiment (measured vs baseline)
Automated runbook actions can be executed via runbook-runner with audit logs, and can be gated behind one-click approval for P0s
Circuit-breaker and load-shed actions revert automatically when SLO burn rate normalizes or via explicit rollback step
Console shows unified incident with per-region contribution and a link to the triggered automation run with logs
tasks: Design dedupe and quiescence algorithm (priority: high)
Implement dedupe in alerting pipeline (pager pipeline: transform)
Add alert score and intent classifier model to group duplicates
Define SLO burn rate thresholds and map to actions (doc in Confluence)
Add automation endpoints to runbook-runner and implement safe guards
Add dashboard widgets: region contribution, burn-rate timeline, automation history
Write on-call playbook and runbook automation approval UX copy
Integration tests: simulate multi-region partial outage and verify suppression and automation flow
Coordinate with platform-ops for private/dedicated customers on allowed automatic actions
runbook_steps: Detect: alert cluster-level error-rate spike in region eu-west-1 with >5% 5m error-rate increase and 12% SLO burn in last 5 minutes
Aggregate: query per-route SLOs and check global burn; collapse duplicate signals into single incident with per-region tags
Score: run intent classifier to determine likely retry storm vs real upstream failure
Decision: if intent_score < 0.4 AND per-route impact < 0.5% of global qps -> quiesce pages for 10 minutes and create summary incident only
If intent_score >= 0.4 OR per-route impact >= 0.5% -> escalate to on-call and surface recommended automated action
Automated action (pre-approved): runbook-runner initiates automatic load-shedding tier 1: reduce non-critical feature traffic by 20%, switch model variant to quantized-x8 for affected routes
Observe: monitor SLO burn and latency for 4 minutes; if improvement > 60% continue, else escalate to manual on-call
Rollback: automated rollback if SLO burn drops below 2x baseline for 10 minutes or manual rollback via one-click in console
Post-incident: attach automation logs, create postmortem task, and adjust quiescence thresholds if needed
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback via console 'Undo Automation' button (calls runbook-runner rollback endpoint)
If rollback fails, trigger circuit isolation to prevent additional config churn and escalate to infra on-call
Fallback: route traffic to global fallback model hosted in dedicated capacity (warm)
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive suppression decreases pages but risks hiding slow-developing issues; mitigation is to keep a low-cost 'summary incident' visible to SRE leads
We intentionally prefer short quiescence windows (10m) with conservative thresholds for first rollout
Pre-approved automated actions limited to reversible, non-destructive operations (traffic steer, model-variant swap, percentage-based shedding). No auto DB schema changes or instance recreation.
Coordination required with Dedicated teams to respect capacity commitments; early experiments limited to hosted deployments
